text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC is only worth it if weight and size matter more to you than lifespan.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle life | About 3,000–6,000 cycles | About 1,000–2,000 cycles |
| Safety | More thermally stable and less prone to thermal runaway | Less stable at high temperatures |
| Weight | Heavier | About 20% lighter for the same capacity |
| Cost over time | Lower cost per cycle, even if the upfront price is similar or higher | Cheaper or lighter at purchase, but wears out sooner |

The cycle-life and weight figures come from [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc). I only read the search-result snippets, not the full pages. [Unplugged Watts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) also concludes that LFP is the better buy for most people. [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) says all 54 power stations in its data set use LiFePO4, so LFP is now standard.

**Choose LiFePO4 if you:**
- want a home backup, RV, or van unit you'll use for years
- cycle it often, for example with solar
- care most about safety and longevity

**Choose NMC if you:**
- carry it a lot, such as for backpacking, camping, or travel
- need the lightest and most compact unit
- will only use it occasionally
